findings.title: Pods are covered by more than one PodDisruptionBudget
findings.cause: PodDisruptionBudgets frontend and web all select 2 pods (web-9fcd6d76c-s4n6k for one): the eviction API refuses a pod that more than one budget covers, so a node drain or cluster upgrade fails on these pods whatever the budgets allow

evidence.what: budget frontend selects pods with tier=frontend
evidence.command: kubectl get pdb frontend -n kd-pdb-overlap -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'

evidence.what: budget web selects pods with app=web
evidence.command: kubectl get pdb web -n kd-pdb-overlap -o jsonpath='{.spec.selector}'

evidence.what: pod web-9fcd6d76c-s4n6k has labels app=web,pod-template-hash=9fcd6d76c,tier=frontend, which every one of those selectors matches
evidence.command: kubectl get pod web-9fcd6d76c-s4n6k -n kd-pdb-overlap -o jsonpath='{.metadata.labels}'

findings.fix: Leave each pod under one budget: delete the extra PodDisruptionBudget, or narrow the selectors so they no longer match the same pods.
